speaker: interviewer
text: Hello Rosa, thank you for joining. Can you hear me?

speaker: interviewee
text: Yes, dear, I can hear you. My granddaughter set this up for me, so if it cuts out, that's her fault.

speaker: interviewer
text: Haha, it sounds great. This is just about your grocery orders, no wrong answers.

speaker: interviewee
text: Good, good.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. Tell me a bit about your household and who does the food shopping.

speaker: interviewee
text: I live with my husband, Bernard, he's retired too. And after school I have my two grandchildren until their mother picks them up. I do the shopping, I always have. I like the market on Tuesdays and the supermarket for the rest.

speaker: interviewer
text: Wonderful. And how did you hear about Shmuber Eats?

speaker: interviewee
text: My granddaughter put it on my phone. I'd turned my ankle stepping off the bus and I was on crutches for nearly three weeks, I couldn't carry a thing. So she said, Grandma, just press here. Now I'm walking properly again I'm at the market on Tuesdays like always.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great, great. Walk me through your last order, from opening the app to putting things away.

speaker: interviewee
text: I pressed the pictures. I put in potatoes, carrots, the chicken, milk, the biscuits the children like, and soap. My granddaughter checked it before I pressed the button. Then a young man brought it to the door and put it on the table for me, which was kind.

speaker: interviewer
text: That's lovely. Was anything difficult in the app?

speaker: interviewee
text: The writing is very small. I had to use my glasses and then the magnifying glass.

speaker: interviewer
text: Noted, text size. And how did you pay for it?

speaker: interviewee
text: My granddaughter put her card in, and I gave her the money in an envelope. That's how we do it.

speaker: interviewer
text: Haha, lovely. Great. How often do you order groceries online?

speaker: interviewee
text: Two or three times, I think.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. Tell me about the last time an item in your order was substituted.

speaker: interviewee
text: The biscuits. They brought a different kind, with chocolate, and the children were delighted, so I didn't complain.

speaker: interviewer
text: Did you know before the delivery came?

speaker: interviewee
text: No, I don't think so. My phone makes a noise sometimes, but I don't always know what it wants.

speaker: interviewer
text: Haha. Great. How did you pick the delivery window last time?

speaker: interviewee
text: My granddaughter picked it. Ten to twelve in the morning, I think, because I'm always home in the morning.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. What would you think of a monthly delivery pass, and what would you pay for it?

speaker: interviewee
text: Every month? No, dear. Bernard would have a fit. We're pensioners.

speaker: interviewer
text: Even if it saved on the delivery fee each time?

speaker: interviewee
text: We don't order enough for that. Maybe two or three a month, if it was nothing.

speaker: interviewer
text: Okay. Great. What did you like most about it?

speaker: interviewee
text: The young man carrying it in. Truly, he was very kind.

speaker: interviewer
text: And what did you like least?

speaker: interviewee
text: The small writing. And the potatoes were very small too, but that's not your fault.

speaker: interviewer
text: Haha. Did the children help you unpack?

speaker: interviewee
text: They ate half the biscuits before I'd closed the cupboard.

speaker: interviewer
text: Haha. Great. On a scale of one to ten, how was it overall?

speaker: interviewee
text: Eight. It was a help.

speaker: interviewer
text: Wonderful. And did your husband use it as well?

speaker: interviewee
text: Bernard? No. Bernard doesn't use his phone for anything except the weather.

speaker: interviewer
text: Haha. And would you use the app again?

speaker: interviewee
text: Perhaps. I'd have to ask my granddaughter to sit with me again, I don't remember all the buttons.

speaker: interviewer
text: Haha. Great. Last question, is there anything about your orders I didn't ask about?

speaker: interviewee
text: No, I think that's everything, dear.

speaker: interviewer
text: Thank you so much, Rosa, it was lovely talking to you.

speaker: interviewee
text: You too. Bye now.
